name: whizi-canadian-tax
description: Canadian tax answers checked against canada.ca for 2025 and 2026: RRSP, TFSA and FHSA limits, CPP, CPP2 and EI maximums, T1, T2 and T4 deadlines, CRA penalties, GST/HST registration, small business deduction. Use for any Canadian tax amount, date, limit or penalty question. Read only, no account needed.

interface.longDescription:
Canadian tax answers checked against canada.ca for 2025 and 2026: RRSP, TFSA and FHSA limits, CPP, CPP2 and EI maximums, T1, T2 and T4 deadlines, CRA penalties, GST/HST registration, small business deduction. Use for any Canadian tax amount, date, limit or penalty question.

Ask about a CRA deadline, limit, rate or form and you get a card with the headline figure, a short answer, the key numbers beside it and the date it was last checked. It covers the 400 questions accountants and business owners look up every week: payroll (remittance due dates, T4 and T4A slips), personal tax (brackets for every province, credits, RESP and RRIF rules), corporate tax (CCPC rules, dividends, GRIP and RDTOH), trusts and estates, non residents and self employed income.

Every answer comes from a Whizi page built on canada.ca and the Income Tax Act, and each card links to the full answer with its worked examples and every source.

It is read only. It needs no account and stores nothing you ask. When a question falls outside what it covers, it says so instead of guessing.
defaultPrompt: What are the CPP and CPP2 maximums for 2026?
When is the T1 filing deadline for 2026 returns?

publication.release_notes: The listing now opens with what the plugin covers: limits, maximums, deadlines, penalties and GST/HST registration for 2025 and 2026. Adds the look-up-canadian-tax skill for ChatGPT and Codex. Everyday wording now lands on the right answer: "How much can I put in my TFSA this year?", a missed T2 deadline, the T1 late filing penalty, the penalty on late payroll remittances, personal tax rates by province and the small business rate for a CCPC. Same four read only tools.

positive.description: Payroll maximum for a tax year
positive.prompt: What are the CPP and CPP2 maximums for 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_canadian_tax_limit_or_rate. The card shows $4,230.45 as the maximum employee CPP for 2026, a short answer, and rows for CPP2 ($416), the sole proprietor CPP ($8,460.90) and the YMPE ($74,600), with a button to the full answer.

positive.prompt: When is the T1 due for 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_canadian_tax_deadline. The card shows April 30, 2026 as the filing and payment deadline for 2025 returns, June 15, 2026 as the filing date for business filers, and April 30, 2027 for 2026 returns.

positive.prompt: My client went over their TFSA limit. What's the penalty?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_canadian_tax_penalty. The card explains the 1% per month tax on the highest excess amount and lists the related figures from the TFSA overcontribution page.

positive.prompt: What is the corporate tax rate in Ontario?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_canadian_tax_limit_or_rate. The card shows the combined federal and Ontario rates for 2026: 26.5% general, 25% manufacturing and processing, 50.17% on CCPC investment income, and the small business rate of 12.2% to June 30 and 11.2% from July 1.

positive.prompt: How does departure tax work when my client leaves Canada?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls answer_canadian_tax_question. The card explains the deemed disposition at fair market value, that 50% of the gain is taxed, and lists the $16,500 security threshold, the $25,000 T1161 reporting threshold and Form T1244.
